description.value: The Bowser Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library opened in 2008 as VIRL's first purpose-built library building, featuring large locally sourced beams and a West Coast architectural style. Situated in this small coastal community along the Island Highway corridor, it functions as a lively community hub offering free WiFi, public computers, a seed library, and a reading nook. Touring cyclists passing through the Bowser area will find a welcoming, no-cost indoor rest space with internet access.

address.value: 6996 West Island Highway, Bowser, BC V0R 1G0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Primary evidence is the VIRL Bowser Branch website, which lists branch features explicitly: 'Free public WiFi' confirms Wi-Fi; the computer stations and feature list do not mention bike parking, washrooms, showers, or device charging. OSM corroborates free WiFi via internet_access=wlan and internet_access:fee=no. No OSM tag or website passage references bike parking, water refill, or washrooms, so those remain null per the absence-is-null rule.
concerns: Required criteria — bike parking, washrooms, and water refill — are not mentioned anywhere on the website or in OSM tags; cannot confirm this location meets minimum WWC thresholds.
Phone number and street address could not be independently confirmed from website content (contact info section was truncated in the fetch).
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The library is a legitimate, open public facility with free WiFi that could be useful to touring cyclists, but none of the three required criteria (bike parking, water refill, washrooms) are confirmed from the website or OSM tags. A site visit or direct contact would be needed to verify basic cyclist amenities before including.
enrichment_extras.notes: Website branch features page explicitly lists: collection of ~8,000 items, free public WiFi, 2 drop-in computers (60-min sessions), word processing, printing & photocopying, reading nook, open jigsaw puzzle table, and seed library. No cycling-specific infrastructure mentioned.
